html:
The OCP Group, founded in 1920 as the Office Chérifien des Phosphates, is the state company that mines Morocco's phosphate rock. Mining began at Khouribga in 1921.

Phosphate is a main ingredient of farm fertiliser, and Morocco, with the territory of Western Sahara, holds around two thirds of the world's known reserves. Under the French protectorate the mines were run as a state monopoly, and they stayed in state hands after independence.

Phosphates and fertiliser are among Morocco's biggest exports, sold to India, Brazil and Africa. The mine at Bou Craa in Western Sahara is one reason the territory matters so much to Morocco. See also the Green March.
sum: The OCP Group, founded in 1920 as the Office Chérifien des Phosphates, is the state company that mines Morocco's phosphate rock. Mining began at Khouribga in 1921.
